title: Compare category totals you can check
summary: Compare three totals in React, inspect their exact values, and verify the server-rendered bar geometry.
job: Compare categories and keep a usable route to the values when the picture is unavailable.
dataShape: One already aggregated, nonnegative total per category, all in the same unit. The synthetic fixture is North 12, South 30, West 18.
fit: Use in an existing Semiotic React application or when structured chart access and schema-guided validation meet an explicit project requirement.
exclusions: A small chart change alone need not justify replacing a working visualization library.
This fixture does not establish that an external source is accurate or that every reader can use the result.

expected: North 12, South 30, West 18; total 60, with South largest.
Three SVG bars retain 12:30:18 proportions and insertion order in both orientations.
The browser data table retains the exact category/value mapping.
An invalid value accessor is refused; the repaired configuration preserves the rows.
unassessed: Underlying source accuracy: this is a synthetic fixture.
Assistive-technology reception and usability with actual readers.
Organic discovery, model preference, and published-package parity.

recovery.symptom: The chart has no useful values after a field was renamed.
recovery.action: Set valueAccessor to the actual numeric field, total, while preserving data. Run the server check and inspect the exact-value table.
recovery.recheck: The bars must encode 12, 30 and 18; a nonempty scene alone is insufficient.

recovery.symptom: prepareChart returned ok, but there is no SVG.
recovery.action: Inject renderChartWithEvidence from semiotic/server in Node authoring code when rendered evidence is required.
recovery.recheck: Inspect evidence and svg explicitly. Without a renderer, ok covers a different set of checks.

continuation.rationale: This project needs React rendering with inspectable category values.
recheck: Category/value mapping, units, order, summary and the accessible table after source or dependency changes.
continuation.loss: An image alone omits the source rows and verification context. Keep the config and fixture when the next reader needs exact values.

update.previousAssumption: A valid configuration or a nonempty render establishes that the values are mapped correctly.
update.action: Run configuration checks, inspect the rendered geometry and compare the category/value table with independent fixture facts.
recheck: Rendering evidence must be present when a render is claimed.
An installed package version different from the packet's packageVersion needs matching guidance.
update.remaining: Source truth and usability with actual readers remain separate obligations.
